reply_text:
I’d fix these before merging. Reviewed `excerpt-helper` (`59856d7`) against `main`; no files changed.

1. **The helpers aren’t connected to cards.**  
   `src/card.js:1–2` still returns `entry.body.trim()`. Neither new helper is called anywhere, so cards continue showing full Markdown bodies rather than plain-text excerpts. The preview path needs to use both helpers.

2. **Short and exact-limit text is incorrectly truncated.**  
   `src/excerpt.js:6–8` always searches for a cut point and appends an ellipsis, even when nothing needs removing:
   - `excerpt('hello', 10)` → `'hello…'`
   - `excerpt('hello world', 11)` → `'hello…'`

   This contradicts the README’s unchanged-text contract. Check whether the text fits before cutting or trimming it.

3. **A word ending exactly at the limit gets dropped.**  
   `src/words.js:2–4` searches only the characters *before* `limit`, excluding a space at that position. `excerpt('one two three', 7)` returns `'one…'`, although `'one two…'` fits the documented boundary rule. The current helper test actually locks in this off-by-one behavior.

4. **Markdown conversion deletes literal content.**  
   `src/plain.js:3` removes every underscore, asterisk, tilde, and backtick without checking whether it is markup. For example, `toPlain('snake_case and https://a_b.test')` becomes `'snakecase and https://ab.test'`. Plain text and code content should retain literal characters.

5. **Common Markdown syntax leaks into the preview.**  
   `src/plain.js:3–4` doesn’t fully flatten Markdown: `'# Heading\n\n- item'` becomes `'# Heading - item'`, and `'![alt](image.png)'` becomes `'!alt'`. Valid links with parentheses in their destination also leave trailing punctuation. A Markdown-aware conversion would avoid these parsing gaps.

**Validation:** all four existing tests pass, but they don’t cover the integration, short/exact-limit inputs, or the Markdown cases above.
